questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A herniorrhaphy and a cleft palate repair are both classified by purpose as:
questions.rationale: Constructive surgery repairs (suffixes -plasty, -orrhaphy, -pexy); ablative removes (-ectomy); palliative relieves symptoms.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Classification of surgery (PDF p. 13)
questions.quote: Suffixesusedare“plasty.""orrhaphy.""pexy."

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A colostomy done to relieve obstruction from an inoperable colon cancer is an example of:
questions.rationale: Palliative surgery relieves distressing symptoms without curing the disease.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Classification of surgery (PDF p. 13)
questions.quote: Palliative.To relieve distressing signs and symptoms,notnecessarily to cure the disease.E.g.,colostomy

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a bleeding peptic ulcer needs surgery within 24–48 hours. By urgency this surgery is:
questions.rationale: Emergency surgery is done immediately; imperative within 24–48 hours; elective can be delayed without harm; optional is requested by the client.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Classification of surgery (PDF p. 14)
questions.quote: Imperative.The procedure should be done within 24 to 48 hours

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For a morbidly obese surgical client, which route is avoided for medications?
questions.rationale: IM injections may not reach muscle in morbid obesity; IV or subcutaneous routes are preferred.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical risk: obesity (PDF p. 14)
questions.quote: Avoid intramuscular injectionsinmorbidly obese individuals.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Obese clients are at higher risk after abdominal surgery for:
questions.rationale: Obesity increases dehiscence, infection and pulmonary complications from hypoventilation, and delays ambulation.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical risk: obesity (PDF p. 14)
questions.quote: Increases potential for postoperative pneumonia and other pulmonarycomplicationsbecause greatlyobesepatients tend tohypoventilate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which oral diabetes drug is usually held before surgery when the client is NPO?
questions.rationale: Metformin is held because of the risk of lactic acidosis while food and fluids are withheld.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical risk: diabetes (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Metformin (Glucophage)shouldbe heldowing to the riskof lactic acidosiswhenfoodandfluidsareheld

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client who drinks heavily every day had emergency surgery this morning. Withdrawal signs are most likely within:
questions.rationale: Anticipate acute withdrawal (delirium tremens) within 72 hours of the last drink.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical risk: alcoholism (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Anticipate theacute withdrawal syndrome（delirium tremens） within72hoursofthelastalcoholicdrink

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client scheduled for elective hernia repair has a fever, cough and sore throat. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: An upper respiratory infection raises the risk of postoperative pneumonia; elective surgery may be postponed.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical risk: pulmonary (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Surgerymayneedtobe postponed if the clienthas upperrespiratory tract infection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During the preoperative interview, a client says she takes ginkgo biloba and garlic capsules. The nurse reports this because they may cause:
questions.rationale: Ginkgo, garlic, ginger and ginseng may impair clotting and increase surgical bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Use of medications (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: Gingkobiloba.gariic,gingerand ginseng may preventblood clotting.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug combination can cause respiratory depression or apnea during surgery?
questions.rationale: Aminoglycosides and some penicillins can block nerve transmission when combined with muscle relaxants.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Use of medications (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: Penicillins andaminoglycosideswhencombinedwithmuscle relaxants may causerespiratory depression

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most common fear of clients awaiting surgery is fear of:
questions.rationale: Uncertainty about the outcome makes fear of the unknown the greatest preoperative fear; accurate information helps.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Psychosocial assessment (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: Fear of the unknown.This is the greatest fear of most patients undergoing surgery

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is scheduled for surgery and the preoperative sedative is due. The consent is not yet signed. The nurse should:
options: Get the consent signed before the sedative
Give the sedative, then get consent
Skip the consent for minor surgery
questions.rationale: Consent must be signed before sedation, voluntarily, while the client is not under the influence of drugs.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Informed consent (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: Theconsent/permitshouldbesigned before theclientreceivespreoperativemedications.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Who is responsible for explaining the risks and possible complications of an operation to the client?
questions.rationale: The surgeon explains the procedure and its risks; the nurse may witness the signature and clarify questions.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Informed consent (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: Theseare expiainedbythesurgeon

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After giving preoperative medication, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Have the client void before premedication; afterwards drowsiness and hypotension raise fall risk.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Day of surgery (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Forpatientsafety,putupsiderails,putcalllightwithinpatient'sreach

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before surgery, the nurse asks the client to remove colored nail polish mainly so that the team can:
questions.rationale: Nail polish interferes with pulse oximetry and observation of nail-bed color for cyanosis.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Day of surgery (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Remove colored nail polish,hearing aid,contact lens,jewelries.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before surgery on the left knee begins, the team pauses to confirm the client, procedure and side. This is the:
questions.rationale: The time-out prevents wrong-patient and wrong-site surgery, a sentinel event.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Best practice (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: practice“TIMEOuT"to checkif the right patient is sent for surgery.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A prophylactic antibiotic is ordered for a client having bowel surgery. It is ideally given:
questions.rationale: Prophylactic antibiotics are given just before or during surgery, ideally before incision, to reach tissue levels in time.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Preoperative medications (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: whenbacterial contamination isexpected,ideallybefore skin incision ismade.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In the supine position on the OR table, which nerve is most often injured if the arm is abducted more than 90 degrees?
questions.rationale: Overabduction of the arm stretches the brachial plexus; pad and position carefully.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical positions (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Themost common injury occurs to thebrachial plexuswhen the amisabducted greaterthan90 degrees.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When placing a client in or out of lithotomy position, the legs should be moved:
questions.rationale: Moving both legs at the same time prevents sacroiliac strain or dislocation and nerve injury.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical positions (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Twomembersofthesurgical teamshouldmovethelegssimultaneously topreventsacroiliacdislocation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During general anesthesia with succinylcholine, a young client develops sudden muscle rigidity, tachycardia and a rapidly rising temperature. The drug of choice is:
questions.rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited reaction to inhalants and succinylcholine; stop the trigger and give dantrolene.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Malignant hyperthermia (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Dantrolene sodium(dantrium)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During induction, the client is unconscious but struggling and shouting. This is which stage of anesthesia?
questions.rationale: Stage II runs from loss of consciousness to loss of lid reflex; keep stimulation to a minimum.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Stages of anesthesia (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Stagell.EXCITEMENTorDELIRiUM-Extendsfromthetimeofloss ofconsciousness to the time of loss oflid reflex.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most common complication right after a spinal anesthetic is given is:
questions.rationale: Sympathetic blockade causes vasodilation and hypotension; keep the client flat, give oxygen and fluids as ordered.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Spinal anesthesia (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Thisisduetointerruptionofthe sympatheticnervous system (SNS).This is the most common and most dangerous

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has a headache that worsens on sitting up after spinal anesthesia. The cause is:
questions.rationale: Spinal headache is from CSF leak; hydrate, keep recumbent and give analgesics as ordered.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Spinal anesthesia (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: This isduetoleakageof CSFfrom the spinal needle puncture hole.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The low, transverse "bikini line" incision used for cesarean section is called:
questions.rationale: Pfannenstiel incision is used for cesarean section; McBurney's for appendectomy; lumbotomy for kidney surgery.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Surgical incisions (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Pfannenstiel Incision.For Cesanan section.Also called”bikini line incision

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An unconscious client arrives in the PACU with an oral airway. The nurse removes the airway when the client:
questions.rationale: Leave the airway until the gag reflex returns; it keeps the tongue from blocking the airway.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 PACU care (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Leave airway inplaceuntil gag reflexhasreturned.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In the PACU, the nurse explains procedures to a client who is not yet awake because:
questions.rationale: Under anesthesia, hearing is the last sense lost and the first regained.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 PACU care (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: In theanesthetized client,senseofhearing isthelasttobelostand thefirsttoretum

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding shows a client is ready for discharge from the PACU?
options: BP within 20 mmHg of preop level
questions.rationale: Criteria include obeying commands, a patent airway without help, BP within ±20 mmHg of baseline, alertness and pink color.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 PACU discharge (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Circulation.Bloodpressureiswithin±20mmHgofthe preoperativelevel.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After surgery, a client has not voided. The nurse expects him to void within about:
questions.rationale: Clients should void within 8–10 hours postop; promote voiding naturally and avoid catheterization if possible.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Postoperative care (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Clientshouldvoid8to10hoursaftersurgery.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: IV fluids are given cautiously in the first day after surgery because:
questions.rationale: Surgical stress raises ADH, so water is retained and fluid overload occurs easily.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Best practice (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Antidiuretic hormone secretionis increased in the immediate postoperative period.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's postop pain is constant over 24 hours. The best way to give the ordered analgesic is:
options: Around the clock at set times
questions.rationale: Scheduled dosing avoids the peaks of the demand cycle and gives better relief; also give before painful activities.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Postoperative pain (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: analgesics should be given around the clock

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client using morphine PCA worries he may overdose. The nurse explains that:
options: A lockout interval limits the doses
He cannot press it more than once a day
There is no limit, so he should be careful
questions.rationale: PCA delivers a set dose with a lockout interval that prevents another dose too soon.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Patient-controlled analgesia (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: Anadjustable“lockout intervalcontrols the frequency of dose administration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client receiving epidural morphine after surgery has itching all over and cannot void. The nurse recognizes these as:
questions.rationale: Epidural opioids cause pruritus, nausea, urinary retention and respiratory depression; naloxone reverses them.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Epidural analgesia (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: Side effects include generalized pruntus,nausea,unnary retention respiratory depression

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which practice increases a postoperative client's risk of deep vein thrombosis?
questions.rationale: Knee gatches and pillows under the knees constrict vessels; massage of calves is also avoided.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Deep vein thrombosis (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: Prevent the use of bedrolls or knee gatches in patients at risk

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Within 48 hours after abdominal surgery, a client has slight fever, tachycardia and diminished breath sounds at the bases. The most likely cause is:
questions.rationale: Atelectasis occurs within 48 hours from shallow breathing; deep breathing, incentive spirometry and ambulation prevent it.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Pulmonary complications (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: Incompleteexpansionoflungorportionofitoccuringwithin48 hours ofsurgery.
